about.title: Rancho Santa Margarita Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Santa Margarita's mix of shopping plazas, HOA-managed common areas, and retail centers along corridors like Santa Margarita Parkway and Antonio Parkway sees steady foot traffic year-round, and with that traffic comes the occasional wet floor, cracked walkway, or poorly lit stairwell. When a property owner or manager knows about a hazard — or reasonably should have known — and doesn't fix it or post a warning, California law may hold them responsible for resulting injuries. These cases often come down to evidence: photos of the hazard, incident reports, and surveillance footage that can disappear quickly if not requested. We handle premises liability claims directly and work on contingency. Our team evaluates your claim and pursues compensation on your behalf without charging you unless we recover damages.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Premises Liability Case

items.title: Proving Notice of the Hazard
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and failed to address it. We can help gather evidence like maintenance logs or prior complaint records to establish that notice.

items.title: Acting Before Evidence Disappears
items.desc: Surveillance footage at retail centers and HOA properties is often overwritten within days or weeks. Prompt legal help can mean the difference between preserved video and a case with no visual record.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present the facts in a way that fairly reflects what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Rancho Santa Margarita?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city facility, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim. It's best to have a case reviewed as soon as possible so this window doesn't close.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility for the accident. Any award is typically reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated entirely. We can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened at an HOA-managed property?
items.answer: Many common areas in Rancho Santa Margarita, including walkways and shared parking areas, are maintained by homeowners associations rather than individual owners. Liability can depend on who had control over and responsibility for maintaining that specific area. This is one of the details we would look into when reviewing your claim.
